warnings: FY2026 (year ending 30 June 2026) is a guided LOSS year (pre-tax loss NZ$340-390m) and is NOT used as the DCF base year or last_fcf. The model instead builds a 10-year component FCF path off FY2025 revenue, starting from a still-depressed Year-1 EBITDA margin and recovering gradually -- see assumptions.base.ebitda_margin_path.

Reported FreeCashFlow in the Metrics CSV (OCF - CapEx) excludes IFRS-16 lease liability principal repayments (~$330-380m/yr, ~5.5% of revenue), a material recurring cash cost of the largely-leased fleet. Owner FCF in this model deducts lease principal in addition to SBC; failing to do so overstates FY2025 'FCF' of $160m into what is actually an owner FCF of approximately -$220m.

Per-share and reported-FCF historical CAGRs are NOT meaningful across FY2020-2022 due to COVID losses and the ~3x dilutive August-2022 rights issue (1.1bn -> 3.4bn shares). Revenue CAGR anchored FY2019 (pre-COVID) to FY2025 (2.6%/yr) is used as the cleanest available growth signal.

10-year (not 5-year) explicit horizon used because owner-FCF margin is still climbing from a negative Year-1 base toward a mature ~2.8% (base case) by Year 8-10; a 5-year horizon would capitalize an unrepresentative, still-negative-to-thin margin.
Bear-case raw model output is a negative equity value; displayed IV is floored at a nominal $0.02/share -- see valuation.bear.floor_note.

inputs.interest_income_note: Air NZ carries NET DEBT (NZ$450m at H1 FY2026), not net cash, so the interest-income-strip rule (for net-cash > 1x FCF base) does not apply; interest income/expense is left inside the WACC-based discounting (unlevered FCF-to-firm methodology) rather than adjusted in the FCF base.
inputs.lease_adjustment_note: Air NZ's reported 'FreeCashFlow' (OCF - CapEx) excludes IFRS-16 lease liability principal repayments, a material recurring cash outflow (~$330-380m/yr, ~5.5% of revenue) for a majority-leased fleet. Owner FCF deducts this in addition to SBC. Reported FY2025 FCF of $160m becomes an owner FCF of -$220m once lease principal ($372m) and SBC ($8m) are deducted.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K style Annual Report FY2025 cash flow statement ('Equity settlements of staff share award obligations', financing activities) and note 19; SBC is immaterial at Air NZ (~0.1% of revenue)
inputs.buyback_cash_note: FY2025 buyback $38m (announced Feb 2025 programme); H1 FY2026 buyback $43m. SBC is immaterial (~$8m/yr) so buybacks more than absorb dilution; shares held flat in projections.
inputs.fy2026_context: FY2026 (year ending 30 June 2026) is guided to a pre-tax LOSS of NZ$340-390m (jet fuel spike to US$150-230/bbl, up to 8-11 aircraft grounded on P&W/Rolls-Royce engine issues, Jetstar Tasman/domestic capacity war). H1 FY2026 net loss was $40m on revenue of $3,444m (EBITDA margin only 9.5%). FY2026 is NOT used as the DCF base year; instead the model builds a mid-cycle owner-FCF path from FY2025 revenue ($6,755m) forward, with Year-1 (FY2027) EBITDA margin still depressed (12.5% base case) before recovering toward a structurally-lower-than-pre-COVID mature margin as fleet renewal, engine normalization and Kia Mau cost savings phase in.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_precovid_anchor_cagr (FY2019->FY2025, 6yr, avoids COVID trough and 2022 rights-issue break)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity, EPS and reported-FCF CAGRs are NOT usable across FY2020-22: COVID losses, a ~3x dilutive 2022 rights issue (1.1bn->3.4bn shares), and revenue-in-advance working-capital swings (FY2023 FCF inflated 34%+ by booking recovery) make per-share and reported-FCF CAGRs meaningless growth signals for this cycle. Revenue CAGR anchored pre-COVID (FY2019) to latest (FY2025) is used as the cleanest available growth proxy at 2.6%/yr, consistent with a mature, low-growth domestic/Pacific network carrier. SBC-adjusted (owner) FCF CAGR could not be computed reliably because owner FCF (after lease-principal deduction) was negative in 4 of the last 5 fiscal years (FY2021, FY2022, FY2024, FY2025) -- see FCF Quality sheet.

base.wacc_rationale: Elevated 11.5% WACC (vs a typical ~8-9% for a mature industrial) reflects: (1) extreme earnings cyclicality -- EBITDA swung negative in FY2022 and margin has ranged from -0.1% (FY2022) to 29.5% (FY2016); (2) direct fuel-price and FX pass-through risk demonstrated starkly by the FY2026 guidance cut (small profit -> $340-390m loss in 3 months); (3) net debt/EBITDA at 2.6x, above the 1.5x-2.5x target range, reducing balance-sheet headroom; (4) ~51% Crown ownership overhang, which provides a funding backstop but also constrains purely commercial responses (fare-setting, cost cuts) and adds political-risk premium; (5) capital intensity/operating leverage of a majority-leased widebody+narrowbody fleet mid-renewal.

bull.narrative: Engine crisis (P&W GTF, Rolls-Royce Trent 1000) resolves faster than guided, full 787/neo fleet available by FY2028; Jetstar competition does not materially erode domestic share; Kia Mau + new-CEO cost programme (~$100m annualised target) fully lands; fuel normalizes toward US$85/bbl; EBITDA margin recovers to 21-21.5% (still below the pre-COVID 23-24% peak, reflecting permanently higher aviation levies).

bear.narrative: Engine groundings persist into FY2028+, Jetstar's Tasman/domestic expansion structurally erodes Air NZ's ~82-85% domestic share, fuel stays elevated, and EBITDA margin stabilizes near 15.5% (barely above FY2024/25 trough). Even with a disciplined capex pull-back (management has flagged a capex plan review), owner FCF remains negative through Year 5, consistent with continued net-debt/EBITDA pressure and dividend suspension persisting for years.

bear.floor_note: Raw DCF output for the bear scenario is negative equity value (NZ$-896m / -$0.28/share) because deep, multi-year cash burn (Years 1-5 owner FCF averaging roughly -$240m/yr) is not fully offset by the modest positive terminal FCF, even discounted at a 13% WACC. A listed equity cannot trade below zero; the negative model output signals a scenario approaching further dilutive recapitalisation (as in the 2022 rights issue) rather than a literal per-share value. Displayed bear IV is floored at a nominal NZ$0.02/share (deep going-concern discount) for dashboard purposes; the unfloored model value is retained in intrinsic_value_model_raw for transparency.

base.note: Entry price sits well below both current price and base-case intrinsic value because base-case owner FCF is deeply negative in Years 1-3 (fleet-renewal capex + heavy lease burden during the current earnings trough) before turning FCF-positive in Year 4. A 15%-IRR buyer must be compensated for several years of cash outflow before payback begins, which is fundamentally different from a steady grower where entry price sits modestly below IV. This is a legitimate output of the formula (interim FCF + terminal value, both discounted at 15%, less net debt, /Year-10 shares), not a calculation error.

sensitivity.note: Base-case FCF path (10yr) and 12x terminal FCF cap held constant; only WACC and terminal growth vary. IV ranges from $0.02 (13.5% WACC / 1.0% terminal growth) to $0.26 (9.5% WACC / 2.5-3.0% terminal growth), underlining how sensitive this cyclical, capex-heavy name is to discount-rate assumptions.

probability_weighted.weight_rationale: Bear weighted above bull (30% vs 20%) reflects the currently-crystallising downside: FY2026 guided pre-tax loss, net debt/EBITDA already above target range, persistent (now multi-year) engine groundings, and an intensifying Jetstar competitive threat to the core domestic profit engine. Base case (50%) assumes gradual normalization consistent with management's own FY2027+ guidance framing (787 deliveries, Kia Mau savings, gradual fleet recovery to CY2027).

outliers_excluded: FY2020-FY2022 (COVID losses, rights issue; P/E n.m., 2021 EV/EBITDA 7.0x on trough EBITDA)
sanity_check.basis_note: Multiples SBC-adjusted on both sides per Step 8c (AIR.NZ SBC is immaterial at ~$8m, so these are close to GAAP figures and will not match screener P/Es for other reasons: screeners use GAAP EPS and trailing periods). Historical multiples computed on FY-end (June) prices from research/AIR.NZ/Reports/historical_multiples.json.
sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip: base IV NZ$0.143 implies P/E 4.0x vs 9.1x avg, P/B 0.24x vs 1.26x max, EV/EBITDA 2.04x vs 7.0x max — all far BELOW history. The model already values AIR.NZ below market (-66.5% base upside) because owner FCF (after IFRS-16 lease principal ~$330-380m/yr) was negative in 4 of the last 5 years and FY2026 is a guided pre-tax loss of NZ$340-390m; no over-valuation fix required.
